conviction_note: This release carries a lot of new information: Q3, the first high-level 2027 EBIT-margin direction and a strategic update for the next cycle, on a name whose last six results-type releases moved 5-18%. So abs_move is 9.0. The sign evidence roughly offsets, so p_up is 52 and the scaled number is +0.36. On the positive side, the guide arithmetic leaves room for a raise, a sourced USD 38m IEEPA one-off will flatter Q3, and a buyback restart is possible. On the negative side, consensus 2027 EBIT (16.3% margin) already sits at the company's implied floor excluding one-offs, and the 2027 silver hedge at ~USD 65/oz means the recent fall in spot to USD 50 does little for 2027. The findings sum (+0.5) and the scaled number agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: Pandora's Q2 report (Note 12) says Phase 2 IEEPA tariff claims of USD 38m (~DKK 245m) were submitted in Q3 and accepted by CBP. Under its stated policy (recognise when virtually certain) a second one-off of that size should land in Q3 reported EBIT. With the DKK 180m from Q2 that makes ~DKK 425m, above the ~100bp (~DKK 335m) built into the 22-23% FY margin guide. Q3 headline EBIT should therefore beat the DKK 845m consensus and the FY margin could edge up on the one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EBIT 1,463 vs a 1,097 consensus, with the DKK 180m refund inside it, and the stock rose 8.53% (771.4 -> 837.2 on 2026-08-13). But underlying EBIT also beat and the guide was raised, and H&M sold a refund-made beat (stage-EU lesson).
findings.why_not_priced: The fact is public, but the DKK 845m Q3 EBIT consensus sits below Q3 2025's 880m and fits an underlying-only estimate. If consensus included the refund it would sit near DKK 1.0bn. Even so the market strips one-offs, so this is sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: The HCA Red Flag note shows consensus also missed the one-off-inflated Q2 (https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/hca-red-flag-pandora-haever-begge-prognoser-og-3-kvartal-ser-lovende-ud-ai). Same mechanism, different source.

findings.finding: The FY26 LFL guide of -2% to +1%, with H1 LFL at 0% and Q3 pre-flagged at mid-single digit, implies Q4 LFL of about 0% or below even at the top of the range. That leaves room to narrow or raise the 0-3% organic guide on any October trading at or above flat. Consensus FY sales of DKK 33.4bn already sit at the top of the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raised in Q2 2026: +8.53% the next day. FY25 guide met plus 2026 guide (Feb 2026): +5.58%. Q1 2026 beat with guide unchanged: +14.31%. Guide cut in Aug 2025: -18.40%. Q3 2025 with the guide merely maintained: -5.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY sales already sit at the top of the guide, so a narrowing is mostly priced. What is not priced is a range raised above 3%, which the arithmetic allows. The Q3 strength was 'helped by phasing', though, which argues the conservative Q4 is deliberate, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: The Proinvestor Danish preview frames the question as 'whether the company maintains or narrows the 0-3% target' (https://proinvestor.com/nyheder/pandora-forventningerne-til-q3-2026-regnskab).

findings.finding: Pandora's 2027 EBIT-margin direction, due 4 Nov, starts from a company floor of >=12% (>=14% excl. transition costs) at USD 82/oz silver plus ~200bp from the 2027 hedge at ~USD 65/oz, i.e. ~14% reported and ~16% underlying. Consensus 2027 EBIT of DKK 5,719m on DKK 35,034m sales (16.3%) already sits at or above that. With 2027 90-100% hedged at USD 65, the fall in silver spot to ~USD 50 (SI=F 50.05 on 2026-11-03), which the stock appears to trade on (+3.8% on 2026-11-02 after silver hit 49.1), adds little to 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2027 margin floor and silver commentary (Jan/Feb 2026) came with -13.01% on the Jan 9 pre-release; Feb 5 then rose 5.58%. The hedge-upside comment in Aug 2026 was part of the +8.53% day.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were reading 2027 off the hedge rather than spot, the stock would not have rallied 3.8% on a 3-dollar fall in silver two sessions before a print whose 2027 cost base is locked at USD 65. Consensus at 16.3% leaves no cushion if the company guides on a reported basis including transition costs. The 2027 bar has a single unnamed provider, so the finding is capped small, and 'at least' language plus possible new levers (platinum, pricing) could beat it.

findings.finding: Pandora said it 'will resume its historical, significant share buyback programmes once the plans to transition to platinum-plated jewellery is further progressed'. The 4 Nov strategic update, the first after the platinum pilot, is a natural place to set that timing. No buyback has run since H1 2026, and leverage targets ~1.5x by year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: buybacks were routine until the 2025-26 silver shock, and Pandora's 2025 payout was 114% of earnings.
findings.why_not_priced: The resumption is conditional and undated, and the Danish and English previews found do not mention a buyback at all. A restart announced tomorrow would be new, but probably below 50% likely, so the expected value is sized small.

outside_window.finding: Platinum-plated wider market test during Q4 2026 and the half-assortment transition in 2027: execution results come after the window
